clue.text: It's repeated the wrong way by an old master

indicators.note: the wrong way means the doubled word is read backwards
repeated means the word it is written twice

parts.note: the word it, with the 's standing for is

explanation.surface: A painting is attributed, perhaps mistakenly, to a famous Renaissance artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repeated' gives ITIT, and 'the wrong way' turns it into TITI, which goes before AN.
explanation.definitionFit: Titian was a great Venetian painter of the Renaissance, and old master is the term for such painters.

clue.text: Absurd misrepresentation of attempt to wrap a piece of clothing

indicators.note: the attempt is wrapped round the other pieces, enclosing them

parts.note: to try is to attempt; here a noun, a go
taken as written
a vest is an undergarment

explanation.surface: Someone describes a ridiculous botched effort to gift-wrap a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: A travesty is a grotesque parody or distorted imitation of something serious.

clue.text: Before close of play, cricket match becomes bad-tempered

indicators.note: the match is placed before the closing letter

parts.note: a Test is an international cricket match

indicators.note: the close of a word is its final letter

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A cricket match turns tetchy just before stumps are drawn.
explanation.definitionFit: Testy is a synonym for irritable or easily annoyed.

clue.text: Study in a library that's emptied so soon!

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the study word sits inside what is left of the library
an emptied word has lost all its middle, leaving only its outside letters

parts.note: taken as written
to read a subject is to study it, as at university

explanation.surface: Someone exclaims that the library cleared out remarkably early.
explanation.definitionFit: Already means by this time, used to express surprise that something happened earlier than expected.

clue.text: Hit and pinched

definitions.meaning: first meaning: struck with a sweeping blow

explanation.definitionFit: The verb swipe means both to strike with a sweeping motion and, informally, to steal.

clue.text: Driver missing in combat

indicators.note: the missing word goes inside the combat word

parts.note: war is armed combat
gone means absent or missing

explanation.surface: A soldier, possibly a driver, has been reported missing in action.
explanation.definitionFit: A wagoner is the person who drives a horse-drawn wagon.

clue.text: Abbreviated greeting after wine and cheese

indicators.note: the shortened greeting comes after the wine

parts.note: port is a fortified wine

indicators.note: cut short, so the greeting loses its final letter

parts.note: a salute is a gesture of greeting

explanation.surface: A cheese-and-wine party where guests exchange curt hellos over the port.
explanation.walkthrough: Port Salut is a mild French cow's-milk cheese, so the surface's 'wine and cheese' is literal.
explanation.definitionFit: Port Salut is a soft semi-hard French variety originally made by Trappist monks.

clue.text: Salesman with a line in expensive-sounding animals

indicators.note: the article and line are placed inside the animals

parts.note: deer sound like 'dear', meaning expensive
taken as written

explanation.surface: A salesman offers a range of pricey-sounding livestock.
explanation.definitionFit: A dealer is a trader who buys and sells goods, such as a car or antiques dealer.

clue.text: Unfaithful wife in part of so-called cage

parts.note: a false lover is an unfaithful one
a humorous term for a wife, from Eve made from Adam's rib

explanation.surface: A cheating spouse is caught in some cage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'So-called cage' points to the ribcage: false ribs are the lower ribs not joined directly to the breastbone.
explanation.definitionFit: False ribs are the lower pairs of ribs in the ribcage that do not attach directly to the sternum.

clue.text: British are mendacious about female monarchs, say

definitions.note: monarchs are one species of the plural answer

indicators.note: the lying phrase goes round the female

parts.note: to utter lies is to be mendacious

explanation.surface: An accusation that Britons tell lies about their queens.
explanation.walkthrough: Monarchs look like kings and queens; they are orange-and-black butterflies.
explanation.definitionFit: The monarch is a well-known migratory species of butterfly, so monarchs are an example.

clue.text: Language that contributes to anger management

indicators.note: the two words each contribute part of the answer, which sits across them

parts.note: the answer runs across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A language said to be useful in therapy for controlling temper.
explanation.definitionFit: German is the official tongue of Germany, Austria and part of Switzerland.

clue.text: Brave conclusions reached by good people of jury

indicators.note: the conclusions of words are their last letters

parts.note: its final letter is the first piece
its final letter is the second piece
its final letter is the third piece
its final letter is the last piece

explanation.surface: A defendant has to face the verdict that a fair-minded jury reaches.
explanation.definitionFit: To brave something is to defy or confront it without fear.

clue.text: Staggered because heavy weight I dropped

parts.note: as can mean since or because
a ton is a heavy unit of weight
taken as written
to shed is to drop or cast off

explanation.surface: A weightlifter staggered because they let a heavy weight fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Staggered here means amazed, stunned with surprise.

clue.text: Mostly err badly about favourite bird

indicators.note: the rearranged letters are placed around the favourite
done badly, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: both words used whole as anagram fodder
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: Someone keeps going wrong in judging their preferred option.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mostly' looks like a deletion signal, but it is part of the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: The storm petrel is a small dark seabird traditionally thought to herald bad weather.

clue.text: Daydreams about large celebrations

indicators.note: the daydreams wrap around the size letter

parts.note: reveries are daydreams

explanation.surface: Someone's daydreams are full of lavish parties.

clue.text: Old family member shouted warning after driving over animal

indicators.note: in a down answer the warning sits over, above, the animal

parts.note: golfers shout 'fore' after driving a ball towards others
a bear is an animal

explanation.surface: A grandparent yelled a warning after running over a creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Driving' sounds like a car on the road, but it is a golf drive.
explanation.definitionFit: A forebear is an ancestor, someone in your family line from long ago.

clue.text: Vehement protesting in the event that ruler enters profession

indicators.note: the condition and ruler go into the profession

parts.note: a vocation is a calling or profession
if means in the event that
ER is Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.definitionFit: Vociferation is loud, insistent shouting or outcry, especially in complaint.

clue.text: Excellent kind of characters needed for TV but not radio

definitions.meaning: first meaning: first-rate, a dated British exclamation of approval

definitions.text: kind of characters needed for TV but not radio
definitions.meaning: second meaning: upper-case letters, as TV is written in them while radio is not

explanation.walkthrough: The 'characters' sound like actors needed for television, but they are letters of the alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Capital can mean splendid, and capital letters are the uppercase form used in abbreviations like TV.

clue.text: Keep confining ring-leader to school again

indicators.note: the keep word encloses the leading letter

parts.note: to retain is to keep
the leader of the word ring is its first letter

explanation.surface: A school keeps the troublemaker locked in for detention.

clue.text: Unexpected attack prior to PM joining President

parts.note: a.m. is the morning, the time before p.m.

explanation.surface: A surprise move before the Prime Minister links up with the US President.
explanation.walkthrough: PM looks like the Prime Minister; it is post meridiem, afternoon.

clue.text: Dash around shopping centre to get details of contract

parts.note: a sprint is a dash
a mall is a shopping centre

clue.text: Short power cut, thank goodness!

parts.note: P is the short form of power in physics
to hew is to cut, as with an axe

explanation.surface: Relief that a power outage lasted only briefly.
explanation.definitionFit: Phew is an exclamation of relief, just like saying thank goodness.

clue.text: In essence, caught lofted shot

indicators.note: caught is placed in the essence word

parts.note: the pith of something is its essence

explanation.surface: A cricket summary: the batsman was caught off a skied stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: C is the cricket scorecard abbreviation for caught. The surface suggests cricket, but the definition is a golf shot.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf a pitch is a short, high approach shot onto the green.

clue.text: Project about story producing tragic heroine

parts.note: to jut is to project or stick out

clue.text: Began hugging learner that's alarmed

clue.text: Lashes out in annoyance

parts.note: the six letters of this word are the anagram fodder

explanation.surface: Someone lashes out in irritation.

clue.text: Part of flower some plant here

parts.note: the answer spans the tail of plant and all of here
